tour.title: Agape: Love as a Chosen Way of Life
tour.intro: This tour starts by clearing away the many meanings we attach to the word “love,” then follows agape from its Christ-shaped center into everyday conduct, Christian community, enemy-love, and a careful look at the Greek words behind Jesus’ conversation with Peter. The clips build from definition to practice without pretending that agape is merely a warm feeling—or that every Greek distinction is as sharp as it is sometimes preached.

steps.why: Begin here because the speaker first names the problem: we “just import into that word” what our culture has trained us to mean by love. He then reframes love as “a settled purpose to behave and choose to act in this way,” which gives the tour its central definition of agape as action, not merely emotion.
steps.episodeTitle: Love Is Not A Black Hole

steps.why: This clip grounds that definition in 1 Corinthians 13. The teacher calls agape “a self-giving commitment to the good of another person, regardless of what I get out of it for myself,” then shows what it looks like: “Love is patient, love is kind,” not jealous, boastful, arrogant, or self-seeking.

Now the focus moves from the abstract definition to the life of a Christian community. The speaker distinguishes agape from simply liking people and describes it as “a regard for the well-being of another person without any consideration for what I get out of it,” a commitment to another’s good “whether I feel like it or whether I benefit from it or not.”

This is the tour’s hardest application: love beyond the friendly or familiar. Reading Jesus’ command to “love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,” the teacher emphasizes that agape is not merely refusing retaliation; it means “to do good for them,” embodying the Father’s generous care for both evil and good.

End with a needed interpretive safeguard. Discussing Jesus’ three questions to Peter, the speaker says the usual claim that agapao means a superior love and phileo an inferior one “way overstates the case.” The passage therefore closes by reminding you that agape matters deeply, while also resisting a simplistic word-study that the teacher says does not fit the conversation.

tour.closing: Taken together, these clips present agape as Christ-shaped, self-giving commitment: something chosen and practiced for another person’s good, patiently within the church and radically even toward enemies. They also leave you with a useful humility: the meaning is carried by the whole teaching and story, not by forcing a single Greek word to do more work than the text supports.

caveats: Clips on ad-inserted hosts (Megaphone: ask-nt-wright, spoken-gospel) can land up to ~2 minutes off against today’s stream. This is a known corpus-wide drift, not a bug in this tour.
A tour is model output over machine transcripts. The "why" text should report what a transcript says; it is not a claim that the speaker is right.

The player streams each episode straight from its publisher. A few hosts (Substack’s CDN, for one) refuse hotlinked requests and the step will say so and offer the URL instead — the clip boundaries are still good, the playback path is not.
